bateria.instruccion: Click the loose battery behind the camera.
bateria.hecho: Done! On the real camera: slide the lock at the bottom, insert the battery with the connectors facing up and release the lock so it stays in place.
bateria.pista: Look for the dark block sitting apart at the back, under the viewfinder.

pantalla.instruccion: Click the screen on the left side to open it. Opening it turns the camera on.
pantalla.hecho: The camera is on. If the screen was already open and the camera is off, press the power button behind it.
pantalla.pista: The screen is closed against the left side of the camera.

tarjeta.instruccion: Behind the screen there's a small door. Click it to open it and insert the card.
tarjeta.hecho: The card is in. On the real camera, follow the shape shown on the guide and push it until it clicks.
tarjeta.pista: The door is on the panel the screen uncovered, toward the back.

formato.instruccion: Press the MENU button on the side panel.
formato.hecho: With the multi-selector on the back, go to “Recording Settings” → “File Format” and choose AVCHD. It's the format the CPMA recommends because it works with any card.
formato.pista: MENU is on the button panel, to the right of the WHITE BALANCE button.

manual.instruccion: Move the AUTO/MANUAL switch on the back to MANUAL.
manual.hecho: Now you can adjust the image yourself. In AUTO the camera decides everything and won't let you change any setting.
manual.pista: It's the lower switch, at the back corner of the left side.

iris.instruccion: Press the IRIS button, the first one in the bottom row.
iris.hecho: Now move the multi-selector to adjust and press it to lock the value. ISO and SHUTTER work the same way. Careful: if you press IRIS again after adjusting, it goes back to automatic.
iris.pista: The IRIS, ISO and SHUTTER row is at the bottom of the left side, below the screen.

nd.titulo: Cut the light with the ND filter
nd.instruccion: It's very sunny and the image looks too white. Move the ND switch on the back up.
nd.hecho: With the ND filter the image is no longer blown out. Each position cuts more light.
nd.pista: The ND switch is on the back, left side, above the AUTO/MANUAL switch.

wb.instruccion: The colors look bluish. Press the WHITE BALANCE button on the side panel.
wb.hecho: On the real camera: choose memory A or B, go to Menu → “Camera Settings” → “WB SET”, fill the frame with something white under the same light and press the multi-selector. Press MENU to exit.
wb.pista: WHITE BALANCE is the left button on the panel, below power.

zoom.instruccion: Push the zoom lever on top of the handle.
zoom.hecho: The optical zoom brings the image closer without moving and without losing quality.
zoom.pista: It's the silver piece on top of the handle, toward the middle.

foco.instruccion: The image is now blurry. Press the AF/MF button on the left side of the lens to focus manually.
foco.hecho: Turning the ring makes the image sharp. If the ring moves the zoom, set the switch next to it to FOCUS. To help you, turn on peaking: Menu → “Display Settings” → “Peaking”.
foco.pista: It's on the left side of the lens, near the body. The FOCUS/ZOOM switch is below it.

audio.instruccion: You connected a microphone through XLR. Move the INPUT switch on the handle to MIC.
audio.hecho: Then, in Menu → “Audio Settings” → “Mic Select”, choose MI SHOE MIC. For supporting shots, switch back to INT MIC to get ambient sound.
audio.pista: The INPUT switches are on the left side of the XLR input block, at the front of the handle.

rec.instruccion: Press the red REC button on top of the handle.
rec.hecho: You're recording! The Z90V has two REC buttons: this one and another on the back. Press REC again to stop.
rec.pista: The red button is on top of the handle, toward the back.
